speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. When did your fever start, and how high has the temperature gotten? Are you experiencing any pain or tenderness in your abdomen or pelvis?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are you experiencing any foul-smelling vaginal discharge or lochia? Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or pain in your legs that might suggest a blood clot?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will examine your abdomen for rigidity and check for costovertebral angle tenderness. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain when you urinate, or is the frequency the only urinary symptom you are experiencing? I need to rule out a urinary tract infection versus endometritis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient did not answer my question about dysuria, so I will focus on the most likely cause given the uterine tenderness. Please check the CBC results immediately and send me a urine analysis to rule out a concurrent UTI. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Doctor
text: While we await the lab results, please describe the character of your vaginal discharge; is it foul-smelling or purulent? I also need to know if you have had any difficulty passing gas or having a bowel movement since delivery.

speaker: Patient
text: Complains of minor difficulty in breathing but denies any urinary pain, headache, vomiting, or diarrhea.

speaker: Doctor
text: The shortness of breath is concerning for a potential pulmonary embolism, so I need to assess your oxygenation immediately. REQUEST TEST: D-Dimer

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the D-Dimer is normal, pulmonary embolism is unlikely, so I am focusing on postpartum endometritis given your uterine tenderness and fever. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the uterine tenderness, fever, and foul-smelling lochia, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis
